title: Material Transfer Studio
description: A product design studio where users preview custom materials on a coffee mug by sampling them from a rotating ShaderBall reference. Users click regions on the ShaderBall to capture material properties, adjust parameters like roughness, metalness, and color tint, then apply the configured material to the coffee mug and export a final turntable preview.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a Material Transfer Studio. Load coffeeMug.glb on the left side and ShaderBall.glb on the right side of the scene using GLTFLoader. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.5, 4) looking at the origin. Add an HDR-style lighting rig with one DirectionalLight, one HemisphereLight, and two RectAreaLights for studio-quality reflections. Use a neutral gray gradient background via scene.background with a Color. Interaction steps: (1) The user clicks on the ShaderBall to select it as the material source, which highlights it with an emissive outline. (2) A floating HTML panel appears with sliders for roughness (0.0-1.0, default 0.3), metalness (0.0-1.0, default 0.7), and a color picker for tint (default white). Validate that roughness and metalness stay within 0-1 range. (3) The user adjusts roughness via the slider and the ShaderBall updates its MeshStandardMaterial in real time. (4) The user adjusts metalness similarly with live preview on the ShaderBall. (5) The user picks a tint color which multiplies with the base material color. (6) The user clicks an Apply to Mug button which animates the material transfer with a ripple dissolve effect using a custom ShaderMaterial that transitions from the mug's original material to the new configured material over 1.5 seconds via a noise-based dissolve uniform. (7) After transfer completes, the user clicks a Turntable Preview button that auto-rotates the mug 360 degrees over 4 seconds while the camera smoothly dollies in by 20 percent, then returns. Add OrbitControls restricted to a 45-degree vertical arc. The mug should sit on a subtle circular shadow-catching plane. Display a small status bar at the bottom showing the current step name. All parameter changes must be validated before applying: clamp numeric values, reject invalid hex colors, and confirm the source material was selected before allowing transfer.
